rationale: Pairing one printed piece with solid pieces keeps the print as the focal point and makes the rest of the outfit easier to coordinate.
limitations: Mixing prints can work well when their scales and colours are matched; this is a gentle default for casual looks, not a restriction on wearing more than one print.

rationale: Straight or tapered trousers under a kurta or kurti keep a clean vertical line below the hem, so the length of the top stays the main shape of the outfit.
limitations: Wide-leg and flared bottoms with a kurta are also common and balanced; this only gives a small lift to straight and tapered cuts, and a user's silhouette preferences come first.

rationale: Collared and mandarin necklines with solid or subtly patterned fabric read as more structured, which keeps the outfit at the same level of formality as most workplaces and formal events.
limitations: Dress codes vary widely by workplace, city and industry; this is a general default and the user's own style and occasion choices take priority.

rationale: Embroidered surfaces add texture and shine, which raises the formality of a look to match festive and wedding occasions.
limitations: Many people prefer understated festive wear, and some families or communities have their own colour and embellishment customs; this is a soft preference that the user's choices override.

rationale: Footwear and accessories in a neutral or metallic shade link back to the rest of the outfit without competing with the main colour, so the look reads as finished.
limitations: A bright shoe or bag can be a deliberate focal point; this only gives a small lift to neutral and metallic options and does not stop accent colours being suggested.

rationale: Regular and relaxed fits with straight or relaxed shapes allow easy movement through a long day or a journey.
limitations: Fit is personal: a user's saved fit preference per category always takes priority over this default, and slim fits remain available.

rationale: A medium contrast between top and bottom looks polished but not stark, which suits a full working day and keeps attention on the person rather than the outfit.
limitations: Many workplaces welcome strong colour; this is a gentle default, and a user's own contrast preference takes priority.

rationale: Higher contrast between pieces, such as a light top with a deep bottom or a bright accent on a dark base, stands out under evening and indoor lighting.
limitations: Low-contrast, tonal outfits are equally suitable for evenings; this is a gentle default, and a user's own contrast preference takes priority.

rationale: A regular fit through the body lets a kurta or kurti hang straight from the shoulder and keeps the side slits and hem falling evenly, which suits occasion and work wear.
limitations: Fit is personal: a user's saved fit preference for ethnic tops always takes priority, and slim and relaxed fits remain available.

rationale: Lehengas are often sold semi-stitched and finished by a tailor, and A-line and flared skirts leave the most room for that adjustment at the waist. The size note shown to the user is never changed by this rule.
limitations: Sizing and stitching vary by retailer; StyleMe does not check product sizes. Straight and fitted lehenga skirts remain available, and the user's silhouette preferences come first.

rationale: Solid bottoms in a neutral colour pair with many different tops, so a few base pieces cover more looks and a shortlist can stay smaller.
limitations: StyleMe does not know prices; budget totals come only from the items and prices the user enters in their shortlist. Printed and coloured bottoms remain available.

rationale: Silk, brocade, georgette, organza and net give sarees and lehengas clearly different weight, drape and sheen, so alternatives drawn from these fabrics differ meaningfully rather than only in colour.
limitations: A user's avoided fabrics are always excluded first. Fabric names describe the typical fabric, not any particular product.

rationale: When the top carries embroidery, zari or mirror work, a solid bottom keeps the embellished piece as the focal point and lets the detail stand out.
limitations: Printed or embellished bottoms are also worn at celebrations; this is a gentle default, not a restriction on wearing more than one pattern.

rationale: An oversized or relaxed T-shirt over straight or wide-leg bottoms keeps one easy, roomy line from top to bottom, the balance most streetwear outfits are built on.
limitations: Fit is personal: a user's saved fit and silhouette preferences always take priority, and fitted T-shirts remain available.

rationale: Gold, antique gold, silver and copper accessories echo zari and other metallic detailing on festive outfits, which links the accessories to the rest of the look.
limitations: Many people prefer coloured, beaded or minimal accessories for celebrations; this only gives a small lift to metallic shades. Metallic names are colour swatches, not claims about metal quality.

rationale: Hand-block prints, kalamkari, leheriya, bandhani and florals give the relaxed, crafted look that a boho style is built around.
limitations: Boho is a broad style and plain pieces fit it too; this is a soft preference that the user's own pattern choices override.

rationale: A slim or regular fit keeps a shirt neat at the waist when tucked in, which matches the structured look expected at formal events and many workplaces.
limitations: Fit is personal: a user's saved fit preference for tops always takes priority, and relaxed fits remain available.

rationale: Wide-leg trousers under a kurta or kurti change the outline of the whole outfit, so offering them alongside straight cuts gives alternatives that differ meaningfully.
limitations: A user's silhouette preferences come first. This only gives a small lift to wide-leg cuts and does not remove straight or tapered ones.

rationale: Jersey-knit T-shirts have some natural stretch, which gives a little more ease within the user's saved size on long journeys. The size note shown to the user is never changed by this rule.
limitations: Stretch varies by product and blend; StyleMe does not check product sizes or fabric content. A user's avoided fabrics are always excluded first, and other fabrics remain available.

rationale: Darker shoes in black, charcoal, navy or brown ground a shirt-and-trousers or kurta look and are the usual choice for offices and formal events, so the outfit reads as finished rather than casual.
limitations: Light and white shoes are common in relaxed workplaces and with some ethnic wear; this is a soft preference, and the user's liked colours and the palette's own colours still come first.
